screening.reach: The full 24-mile Class II Lobatos Bridge (Colorado) to Lee Trail (New Mexico) Ute Mountain run; the New Mexico portion is the campaign coverage focus.
screening.demandSignal: A scenic BLM-managed upper Rio Grande day run with a named public access chain.
screening.scoringSignal: BLM recommends at least 300 cfs. American Whitewater's reach-specific recreational assessment shows 600-2,000 cfs as optimal user preference. Direct USGS 08251500 is at Lobatos Bridge; the route uses a conservative 600-1,500 cfs preferred band with a 2,000 cfs upper scoring guard.
screening.accessAndSeason: BLM names Lobatos Bridge, Stateline and Lee Trail. Private boaters must reserve in advance. The New Mexico segment is closed April-May. BLM warns of erratic winds, limited camps and a steep primitive quarter-mile carry at Lee Trail. The current BLM page and older corridor plan differ on daily launch cap; confirm the active cap with Taos Field Office.
screening.resolved: BLM segment guide plus USGS/American Whitewater flow sources cleared access and scoring blockers. AW's Lee access feature coordinate is about 303 ft off mapped water and outside NHD polygons, so the route uses a nearby in-channel Rio Grande coordinate at the designated Lee Trail reach end.
screening.remainingCaveat: The launch is in Colorado, though the route crosses New Mexico and terminates at a New Mexico BLM access. The state field is New Mexico and route copy states the cross-border access plainly.

decision: Add the scored 24-mile Ute Mountain route with direct Lobatos telemetry and a conservative preference band. Keep reservation-cap language current by directing users to BLM confirmation; classify camping as none and document wind, closure, remote-access, and take-out carry hazards.
